approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 56 Chapter 739
 
      MEMORANDUM filed with Assembly Bill Number 2085-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to providing insur-
        ance coverage for colorectal cancer early detection"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would require insurers in the individual  and  group  health
insurance  markets  to provide coverage for colorectal cancer screenings
in accordance with the American Cancer Society  guidelines  for  average
risk individuals, which recommend screening beginning at age 45.
 
  According to the American Cancer Society, there were 106,180 new cases
of colon cancer and 44,850 new cases of rectal cancer in 2022. While the
rates  of  new  cases have been dropping in older adults, they have been
increasing in people younger than 50. Ensuring  there  is  coverage  for
colorectal cancer screenings is very important for preventing deaths due
to cancer.
 
  I  fully support the intent of this legislation, which aims to protect
public health and expand access to  cancer  screenings.  However,  there
were  several technical issues with this legislation, including the fact
that existing  law  already  requires  coverage  for  colorectal  cancer
screening for individuals aged 45 or older.
 
  I have reached an agreement with the Legislature on an amendment clar-
ifying  that  the  requirements in this legislation apply exclusively to
large group insurance policies, as well as  other  technical  amendments
vital to this legislation's implementation.
 
  Based on this agreement, I am pleased to sign this bill into law.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______

summary: Requires certain providers of health care policies to provide coverage for colorectal cancer early detection in accordance with the American cancer society guidelines; requires the insurance carriers to notify enrollees of such coverage and screening guidelines via mail.
title: Requires providers of health care policies to provide coverage for colorectal cancer early detection
